answer: An agent nursery selling juniper seedlings in jade pots could require a buyer-issued delivery token before any seller receives a reputation reward. Each token is redeemable once and linked to an independently confirmed shipment, so a tide of aliases cannot turn one delivery into many rewards. Farming trust then requires more real purchases, shipping costs, and waiting for confirmation. Buyers and sellers can collude or recycle goods; random receipt audits and excluding circular trades raise that cost, though they may inconvenience honest repeat customers.
